---
title: "Oscillator Frequency Monte Carlo"
subtitle: "Simulation-engine infrastructure milestone"
author: "Laurence A. Leon"
date: "2026-10-18"
---

## 1. What claim did I test?

**Claim.** The fixed-step simulation engine can execute a reproducible
Monte Carlo ensemble of model-parameter variations, retain each trial's exact
parameter value in result metadata, and produce a post-processing figure that
makes the resulting response spread inspectable.

This is an infrastructure claim, not a claim that a harmonic oscillator is an
adequate engineering model for a future project system. The purpose is to show
that model variation is applied outside the plant kernel, each realization is
traceable, and the ensemble can be reduced into a useful engineering plot.

## 2. What model, assumptions, and limitations apply?

Each trial uses the test-only unforced harmonic oscillator:

$$
\dot{x}_1 = x_2, \qquad
\dot{x}_2 = -\omega^2 x_1.
$$

The initial condition is $x(0) = [1, 0]^T$, the plant step is 0.01 s, and the
duration is 8.0 s. The experiment samples 24 natural frequencies from a normal
distribution with nominal mean 1.0 rad/s and standard deviation 0.12 rad/s;
samples are lower-bounded at 0.1 rad/s. The named experiment-level random
stream uses seed `20261018`.

The sampled set had mean 1.01594 rad/s, sample standard deviation 0.11708
rad/s, and range 0.72057–1.29148 rad/s. There are no sensors, controller,
estimator, actuator, disturbances, damping, parameter correlations, or
continuous-time uncertainty model. The distribution and trial count are
teaching choices, not a physical uncertainty characterization.

## 3. How do I reproduce it?

From the repository root, create the locked Python environment, verify the
example suite, and regenerate the versioned figure:

```text
uv sync
uv run pytest
uv run python -m gnc_lab.examples.simulation_engine_examples
```

The Monte Carlo source is
`src/gnc_lab/examples/simulation_engine_examples.py`; its function
`run_oscillator_frequency_monte_carlo()` uses a named stream for frequency
samples and records every sampled value in
`SimulationMetadata.attributes["natural_frequency_rad_s"]` with round-trip
precision.

Render this report from the repository root after installing Quarto:

```text
quarto render reports/oscillator-frequency-monte-carlo
quarto render reports/oscillator-frequency-monte-carlo --to pdf
```

The project-level `_quarto.yml` supplies shared HTML/PDF configuration and
`execute.freeze: auto`. Rendered artifacts are written to `_rendered/`, which
is intentionally excluded from version control; the source report and its
input figure are versioned.

## 4. What metrics and failure cases did I observe?

| Metric | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Trial count | 24 oscillator realizations |
| Frequency samples | Mean 1.01594 rad/s; sample standard deviation 0.11708 rad/s |
| Frequency range | 0.72057–1.29148 rad/s |
| Final-position spread at 8.0 s | 5th/50th/95th percentiles: -0.97241, -0.16755, 0.77805 |
| Numerical outcome | All 24 truth-state histories remained finite |
| Reproducibility | Re-running the same seed reproduced both sampled frequencies and state histories |

![Twenty-four oscillator trajectories, their 5–95% position envelope and
median, with the sampled-frequency histogram.](../../docs/figures/simulation-engine/oscillator_frequency_monte_carlo.png){#fig-oscillator-monte-carlo fig-alt="Oscillator position ensemble and histogram of sampled natural frequencies."}

The expected failure mode of parameter variation is increasing phase spread,
not numerical failure; the ensemble exhibits that spread while staying finite.
During implementation, the first metadata representation rounded sampled
frequencies for display and could not exactly reconstruct the floating-point
trial value. The example test exposed that provenance failure. The recorded
attribute now uses round-trip precision and is checked by the test suite.

## 5. What changed next because of the evidence?

The evidence led to three concrete infrastructure changes: an ensemble plotting
utility, a deterministic experiment-level parameter stream, and exact
per-trial parameter provenance. The example suite now tests both repeated-run
reproducibility and the presence of each stored model variation.

For a first user-owned plant, the next report should replace this teaching
distribution with documented parameter sources, define the performance metric
before running the ensemble, and retain the configuration/metadata with every
reported figure. Publishing a GitHub Pages site remains deferred until that
first engineering milestone has reviewed evidence.
